newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Russia sugar quota seen bad for Ukraine producers.
newsitem.headline: Russia sugar quota seen bad for Ukraine producers.

text.p: Plans in Russia to restrict refined sugar imports from Ukraine to 1.15 million tonnes a year are bad news for producers already facing tough times, the industry's most senior official in Kiev said on Thursday.
"We are not entirely satisfied with having a quota imposed on us," said Olexander Bohatarenyk, deputy head of the state sugar concern UkrSukor. "This is a small amount for Ukraine."
He said producers of sugar beets were already struggling and workers were being paid in sugar.

Russia's Itar-Tass news agency quoted deputy minister Oleg Davydov as saying the Foreign Trade Ministry had sent an order to the government setting white sugar imports at 1.5 million tonnes a year including 1.15 million tonnes from Ukraine.
It did not say when the quota, which must be approved by the government, would be introduced.
"During Soviet times we gave Russia up to four million tonnes of refined sugar every year," Bohatarenyk said. "We could have sold Russia 1.5 million tonnes this year."
Bohatarenyk suggested that the new quota would be increased because Russia did not provide enough for itself.
"Russia produces two million tonnes a year, plus it imports 1.5 million tonnes. It will need more sugar than this, and it's not clear where they'll get it from," he said.
Davydov was quoted as saying that the quota would be temporary and was meant to give Russian producers a chance to get used to competition.
Russia says cheap Ukrainian sugar has flooded the market and put pressure on domestic producers.
Ukraine expects to refine 2.6 million tonnes of sugar this year, Bohatarenyk said, from a low net beet harvest forecast at 26 million tonnes -- down from last year's 30 million tonnes.

Ukrainian sugar was selling at 720 hryvnia ($385) a tonne on the local market mainly due to plenty of refined sugar left over from last year's beet harvest, Bohatarenyk said. Last year sugar fetched $450-460 per tonne.
